subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should OpenClaw make periodic memorySearch.sync.intervalMinutes default-on as the watcher-failure safety net, or keep it opt-in and rely on search-time/manual recovery paths?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but changing an existing default/fallback surface can affect upgrades and background provider work, so automation should not choose the product tradeoff alone.

options.title: Approve default-on fallback after repair
options.body: Land the linked PR once interval dirty marking is scoped correctly and maintainers accept the 30-minute default as the upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep interval sync opt-in
options.body: Keep the 0 default, document intervalMinutes as the supported workaround, and close the linked PR if the shipped zero-hit retry is considered sufficient.

options.title: Ask for another recovery design
options.body: Keep this issue open for a watcher health or doctor-style repair that avoids changing the default periodic sync behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve default-on fallback after repair
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR once interval dirty marking is scoped correctly and maintainers accept the 30-minute default as the upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory index and SQLite-state work makes vincentkoc the best available routing owner for the freshness/default tradeoff.
